seo.title: Common Multiples of 4 and 6 - LCM 12 Math Speed Challenge
seo.metaDescription: Click all common multiples of 4 and 6 on a 100-tile grid. Practice least common multiple (LCM) concepts and avoid the common product trap.
seo.intro: A common mistake students make is multiplying 4 by 6 to get 24, assuming 24 is the smallest shared multiple. In reality, because 4 and 6 share a common factor of 2, their least common multiple (LCM) is 12. Consequently, all common multiples of 4 and 6 are multiples of 12 (12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 96). This speed clicker teaches students to spot shared multiples efficiently. Fluency Development: When students engage in timed identification on a 100-number grid, they move beyond manual finger-counting and transition into visual pattern synthesis. Developing automaticity with this specific math concept reduces cognitive load during multi-step problem solving, long division, and algebraic equation manipulation.
seo.howToPlay: Locate and click every number that is a multiple of both 4 and 6. Correct selections turn green with checkmarks. Incorrect tiles flash red and penalize 2 seconds from the clock. Find all 8 common multiples to win. Keyboard and Accessibility Controls: Students can use a touchscreen, trackpad, mouse, or keyboard arrow keys to navigate between tiles. Pressing Space or Enter activates the focused tile. Wrong clicks temporarily flash red with an X icon and subtract 2 seconds, but remain unlocked so learners can self-correct without getting stuck.
seo.teacherNotes: Use this example to contrast multiplying two numbers (4 x 6 = 24) with finding their actual least common multiple (LCM = 12). Classroom Implementation Ideas: Use this interactive grid during the first five minutes of math instruction as an energetic bell-ringer or daily warm-up. Teachers can project the screen onto an interactive whiteboard for whole-class competitive rounds, or assign the canonical link directly into Google Classroom for independent Chromebook math station rotations.

faq.q: Why is the LCM of 4 and 6 equal to 12 rather than 24?
faq.a: Because both 4 and 6 share the prime factor 2. Using prime factors: 4 = 2^2, 6 = 2 x 3. The LCM takes the highest power of each prime: 2^2 x 3 = 12.

How does mastering click common multiples of 4 and 6 support higher-level math standards?
faq.a: Building speed and accuracy with click common multiples of 4 and 6 directly strengthens mental arithmetic and numerical reasoning. When foundational number facts become second nature, students can dedicate their active working memory to advanced problem-solving strategies, fraction equivalence, and multi-step word problems.
